question.question: According to the 2018 pediatric PN fluid guideline, which care setting can increase neonatal insensible water loss?
choices: Phototherapy with care under an open radiant warmer
Care in a double-wall incubator with high ambient humidity
Mechanical ventilation with warmed, humidified respiratory gases
Additional waterproof covering in a double-wall incubator
question.rationale: The guideline identifies phototherapy and open radiant warming as factors that can increase water loss. Humidity, double-wall incubators, waterproof coverings, and warmed, humidified respiratory gases can reduce losses in the described settings. Reassess actual hydration and electrolytes rather than applying an automatic fluid increase.

teachingReview.heading: Build a complete fluid ledger
teachingReview.body: Maintenance equations are starting estimates. Incubator losses, respiratory support, fever, diarrhea, ostomy or fistula output, drains, kidney function, medications, phototherapy, edema, and concurrent infusions can change the plan. Count nutrition, medicines, carrier fluids, flushes, blood products, and enteral intake in the same daily ledger.
clauseSource: fluid2018 PDF2–7: care environment, renal/edema/fluid retention, fever/respiratory losses and monitoring; PDF3 drains/fistula/ileostomy output
trophamine2020 PDF5–8: diarrhea/fistula/drainage losses and individualized maintenance/replacement

Existing complete pedpn-007 source evidence in pediatric-parenteral-nutrition-development-delivery-review.json: administered PN, medication/carrier/flush/blood/enteral ledger; bookPDF158 and previously reviewed ASPEN administration/intake-output references reused

teachingReview.heading: Advance according to response
teachingReview.body: Infants have higher glucose utilization per kilogram than adults, partly because their brains are large relative to body mass. Glucose also contributes energy for growth. These physiologic needs do not establish a fixed GIR: glucose utilization, endogenous production, and the prescribed infusion rate are different quantities. Advance according to energy needs and glucose trends, accounting for insulin exposure, sepsis, corticosteroids, stress, hepatic glucose handling, respiratory status, and every dextrose source. Excess delivery can cause hyperglycemia, liver fat accumulation, and increased carbon dioxide production. A reference range is not an automatic target, and suspected metabolic disorders require a specific plan.
clauseSource: pes2015 PDF2: infant/child brain-to-body ratio and higher per-kg utilization
carbs2018 PDF2–5: growth energy, production/utilization distinction, all-source glucose, titration and hyperglycemia/steatosis/CO2 consequences, special metabolic disorders
hyperglycemia2018 PDF2–4: stress/sepsis/steroid/respiratory distress and hepatic/endogenous production risk; insulin exposure and glucose monitoring

teachingReview.heading: Do not impose blanket protein restriction
teachingReview.body: Renal or hepatic dysfunction does not establish a universal 1 g/kg/day protein ceiling. The 2023 Pediatric Renal Nutrition Taskforce guidance for children with acute kidney injury accounts for growth, illness-related catabolism, and dialysis losses, which are greatest with continuous kidney replacement therapy. With markedly rising urea, assess energy adequacy and consider a temporary adjustment; do not persistently restrict protein to postpone dialysis. Wound severity also matters: extensive burns can raise needs. Hepatic impairment requires assessment of amino-acid and ammonia handling and product contraindications. For example, the cited 2020 TrophAmine label contraindicates hepatic coma and directs discontinuation and reassessment if hyperammonemia symptoms develop. Use disease-specific guidance and the current product label; neither automatic restriction nor automatic escalation is appropriate.
clauseSource: renal2023 section6.1–6.4 and full rationale: growth/illness catabolism/CKRT losses, energy adequacy and temporary adjustment for rising urea, no persistent protein restriction to delay KRT
trophamine2020 PDF5–8: extensive-burn protein needs, hepatic amino-acid/ammonia handling, hepatic coma contraindication and stop/reassess symptomatic hyperammonemia
